terms.definition: The total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom.
terms.examiner: The atomic (proton) number is the number of protons in the nucleus.

terms.definition: Atoms with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
terms.examiner: Isotopes of an element have the same electron configuration, so the same chemical properties.

terms.definition: The average mass of an atom of an element, relative to one-twelfth of the mass of an atom of carbon-12.
terms.examiner: "Average mass of an atom" and the carbon-12 comparison are both needed. From a mass spectrum it is the weighted mean of the isotopic masses.

terms.definition: The average mass of a molecule, relative to one-twelfth of the mass of an atom of carbon-12.
terms.examiner: Use relative formula mass for ionic compounds.

terms.definition: The energy required to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms to form one mole of gaseous 1+ ions.
terms.examiner: "Gaseous" is needed, and the equation must have state symbols: X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.

terms.definition: A high-energy electron from an electron gun knocks an electron out of each particle to form a 1+ ion.
terms.examiner: Used for elements and substances of low formula mass. X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.

terms.definition: The sample is dissolved in a volatile solvent and injected through a needle at high voltage, so each particle gains a proton to form a 1+ ion.
terms.examiner: Used for substances of higher molecular mass. The peak is at Mr + 1 because of the added H⁺.
